articles.title: Super Sunday for India! Lakshya Sen ends year-long title drought as PV Sindhu completes Hylo Open double delight
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian badminton enjoyed a memorable Super Sunday at the Hylo Open 2026 as Lakshya Sen ended his year-long wait for a BWF World Tour title,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian badminton enjoyed a memorable Super Sunday at the Hylo Open 2026 as Lakshya Sen ended his year-long wait for a BWF World Tour title, joining PV Sindhu in winning the men's and women's singles crowns at the Super 500 tournament in Saarbrücken, Germany.Lakshya produced a commanding performance to defeat Indonesia's fourth seed Jonatan Christie 21-17, 21-10 in the men's singles final, bringing an end to his title drought that had stretched back to the Australian Open in November 2025.Earlier, double Olympic medallist Sindhu had clinched the women's singles title with a dominant 21-12, 21-14 victory over Denmark's Line Højmark Kjærsfeldt. The two straight-game victories ensured India walked away with both singles trophies, capping a remarkable campaign at the USD 500,000 event.For Lakshya, the victory was particularly significant after a season disrupted by injuries and inconsistent performances. The 25-year-old had reached the All England Championships final earlier this year but had struggled to maintain that level in subsequent tournaments.Lakshya dominates Christie to end title droughtThe men's singles final initially developed into a closely fought contest, with both players engaging in fast-paced rallies and exchanging powerful smashes.Lakshya made an aggressive start to take an 8-4 lead, using sharp cross-court angles and attacking strokes to push Christie around the court. The Indonesian, however, responded with a five-point run to move ahead 9-8.The Indian recovered his composure and gradually regained control through solid defence, deceptive net play and well-directed smashes. He held his nerve in the closing exchanges to take the opening game 21-17.The second game was far more one-sided. Lakshya raised his intensity, capitalising on Christie's unforced errors while controlling the rallies with excellent movement and shot selection.The Indian repeatedly neutralised the Indonesian's attacking strokes and turned defence into counter-attacking opportunities. Christie struggled to find answers as Lakshya extended his advantage and eventually sealed the game 21-10 to secure the title.The victory also levelled Lakshya's career head-to-head record against Christie at 4-4.Sindhu leads India's double title celebrationSindhu had set the tone for India's title-winning Sunday by defeating Kjærsfeldt in the women's singles final.It was Sindhu's second title of the season after her Japan Open triumph in July. She had also finished runner-up at the French Open last week, making the Hylo Open victory another significant boost to her late-season campaign.The Indian's title run also earned her 9,200 ranking points, keeping her in contention for qualification for the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals.Lakshya had also spoken about rediscovering his rhythm after an injury-interrupted period following his semifinal victory."I've had a few niggles here and there, and I was out for some time. At certain tournaments, I wasn't really 100 per cent. But I'm happy with the way I've played here. It's a really good confidence booster because I haven't played this many matches in a row over the last couple of months," he had said."I'm really happy to reach another final. Since the All England Championships, I think this is the first time I've felt that I was playing really well again. I can feel myself getting back into rhythm and playing good badminton."With Sindhu and Lakshya both finishing on top of the podium, India secured a memorable double at the Hylo Open, with the two leading shuttlers delivering a timely boost ahead of the closing stretch of the badminton season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: en el minuto 75 José Luis Munuera Montero señaló el punto de penalti a favor del Racing y luego cambió su decisión tras consultar el monitor del VAR. articles.title: 'You are horrible': Rex Ryan rips into Ashton Jeanty after Raiders RB's Jets criticism
articles.summary: Ahead of Jets vs. Raiders on Sunday, New York's former head coach was not happy with Jeanty's choice of words.
articles.body:
Ahead of the Raiders ' matchup with the Jets this week, star running back Ashton Jeanty had some rather interesting words about the defense he would be facing.

Jeanty, who has managed just 3.1 yards per carry so far this season but been effective as a receiver, took a dig at the Jets' tackling ability before he lined up in the backfield against them on Sunday.

On ESPN, former Jets head coach Rex Ryan wasn't happy about Jeanty's comments, ripping into the former Heisman runner-up by calling him "the worst draft pick" among running backs in the last 20 years.

Here's what Ryan said about Jeanty's criticism of the Jets' defense.

Rex Ryan rips into Ashton Jeanty after Jets criticism

Before Sunday's game, Jeanty was talking about the Jets' defense earlier this week and what the Raiders will be able to do.

He noted there are "a couple of guys that don't really tackle" for New York, though he didn't want to say "names."

In response on ESPN, Ryan first broke down some strong tacklers on the Jets' defense, including Demario Davis, before ripping into Jeanty.

The former coach said that if he were still coaching, he would approach Jeanty and tell him, "We are not going to try to take you out of the game."

"Why? Because you are horrible. You're about the worst draft pick of the last 20 years, I think, as a running back," Ryan said. "You stink. You're averaging 3.1 yards per carry. ... It's on you, my friend."

Ryan has never been shy about his football thoughts — especially when it comes to his former Jets franchise.

Of course, it's likely an exaggeration to call Jeanty the worst running back draft pick of the last 20 years; he's been good for the Raiders, but not quite great. As a rookie, he finished with 975 rushing yards and 10 total touchdowns. So far in 2026, he's been extremely inefficient as a rusher, but effective as a receiver.

Jeanty has begun to cede backfield work to his backup, rookie Mike Washington Jr. If he can't perform against the Jets on Sunday, Ryan may just have more words for the Raiders' second-year back.

articles.title: Official Juventus team to face Napoli – Muani Woltemade start
articles.summary: Juventus face Napoli in a match that could be crucial for Luciano Spalletti as he looks to save his job and avoid back-to-back league defeats. This is the te...
articles.body:
Juventus face Napoli in a match that could be crucial for Luciano Spalletti as he looks to save his job and avoid back-to-back league defeats. This is the team put out by the manager as he looks to get Juve back to winning ways.

This should be a match between two title challengers, but on paper it is a game between two top teams that have both struggled with inconsistency this season. Napoli are not the best travellers, but Juventus still need to raise their level if they are to secure a positive result.

Juventus have time to turn their season around, and this game could serve as a turning point. The team need to win and, at the very least, avoid another defeat in front of their own fans at the Allianz Stadium.

The players lack confidence, and fans will hope that the training retreat imposed by Spalletti will help them improve. The retreat is intended to bring the squad together and prepare them for a match that carries significant importance for the club.

If Juventus fail to get a result and Napoli leave Turin with all three points, it could create further problems for the club in their upcoming matches. Spalletti's position could come under even greater scrutiny, particularly if the team do not improve before the next international break.

Juventus need their players to compete at their best if they are to beat Napoli. The squad have the quality to get a result, but they must show greater belief and consistency than they have in recent weeks.

Spalletti knows what is at stake, and the outcome of this game could shape the direction of Juventus' season. A win would ease the pressure and provide a platform to build on, while another defeat could deepen the club's difficulties and raise further questions about the manager's future.

articles.title: Five Big 12 teams ranked in US LBM Coaches Poll after Week 9 action
articles.summary: Utah rises to No. 4 in the US LBM Coaches Poll after Week 9, while Ohio State tumbles to No. 10. Five Big 12 teams remain ranked in the Top 25.
articles.body:
Colorado finally got back in the win column after five straight losses, taking down Kansas State in overtime , 27-24. Despite the win, Colorado is far from being considered for the latest US LBM Coaches Poll , but the Big 12 Conference holds steady with five teams in the poll after Week 9 results.

Utah took care of business on the road at Cincinnati and moved up one spot to No. 4, the top ranking in the Big 12. BYU and Texas Tech moved up one spot each to No. 8 and No. 13, respectively. Houston, which was on a bye this week, moved up one spot to No. 18. Arizona remained in the poll at No. 22 despite a loss to Texas Tech.

Oklahoma State and Cincinnati were the two teams in the receiving-votes category, with the Cowboys getting nine votes and the Bearcats one this week.

Elsewhere in college football, the top 10 saw a slight reshuffle behind No. 1 Miami. Georgia is the new No. 2, followed by Indiana , Utah, and UCLA to round out the top 5. Ohio State fell eight spots to No. 10 following its road loss to USC. The Trojans moved up eight spots after the win.

New Mexico is the lone new team in the poll, taking the No. 25 spot after Florida dropped out.

Here is the full US LBM Coaches Poll as we head into Week 10.

South Carolina 91; Florida 81; UTSA 76; Duke 76; Virginia Tech 53; Oregon 41; Minnesota 10; Oklahoma State 9; Liberty 6; North Texas 4; Wisconsin 3; Memphis 2; North Dakota State 1; Nebraska 1; Cincinnati 1

articles.title: Liverpool vs Arsenal: The tactics board - Kai Havertz proves the difference as Mikel Arteta wins the central duel
articles.summary: Arsenal secured a disciplined 1-0 victory at Anfield through a clinical Kai Havertz strike and a masterclass in defensive organisation. Mikel Arteta’s side s...
articles.body:
Arsenal secured a disciplined 1-0 victory at Anfield through a clinical Kai Havertz strike and a masterclass in defensive organisation. Mikel Arteta's side successfully nullified Liverpool's high-octane build-up, restricting the hosts to just four shots on target despite conceding the lion's share of possession.

This was a fixture defined by spatial control and the suppression of transition. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool entered the contest aiming to exploit the half-spaces and overwhelm Arsenal with a fluid 4-2-3-1 that often resembled a 3-2-5 in possession. By pushing Milos Kerkez high and asking Florian Wirtz to float between the lines, Iraola sought to pull Arsenal's defensive block out of shape, creating avenues for Alexander Isak to exploit the depth. The objective was clear: high-intensity pressing to force errors and rapid verticality to punish them.

Conversely, Arteta prioritised central compactness and structural discipline. Knowing the volatility of Anfield, Arsenal operated in a highly coordinated 4-2-3-1 that transitioned into a mid-block 4-4-2 when Liverpool's centre-backs had the ball. The strategy was not to dominate the ball - as evidenced by their 44% possession - but to control the zones where Liverpool are most dangerous. By deploying Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes as a double pivot, Arteta erected a barrier that effectively quarantined Liverpool's creative engines, allowing Havertz to act as the primary outlet in transition.

Iraola opted for a 4-2-3-1 formation that relied heavily on the technical proficiency of Alexis Mac Allister and the teenage Trey Nyoni in the pivot. The tactical blueprint was designed to invite Arsenal's press before bypassing it with diagonal balls to the flanks, particularly targeting the width provided by Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo. Liverpool's build-up pattern involved Virgil van Dijk acting as the primary distributor, looking to find Wirtz in the pockets. However, the pressing triggers - usually activated when the ball was played into Arsenal's full-backs - were frequently bypassed by David Raya's long distribution.

Defensively, Liverpool maintained a high line, with Ronald Araujo and van Dijk tasked with managing the space behind them. The plan was to squeeze the game into the middle third, but the lack of pressure on Rice in the 16th minute proved fatal. Despite Liverpool's 56% possession and 18 total shots, their inability to generate high-quality chances was a direct result of their predictable wide delivery. With 33 crosses attempted, Liverpool fell into the trap of playing around the Arsenal block rather than through it. The host's xG of 1.31 suggests they created moments of danger, but only registering four shot on target highlights a significant failure in the final third execution against a well-drilled low block.

Arteta's side mirrored the 4-2-3-1 formation but with vastly different functional roles. The key was the defensive screening provided by Rice and Guimaraes. Their primary instruction was to shadow Wirtz and prevent Mac Allister from dictate play. Arsenal's defensive shape was exemplary; they recorded 26 interceptions, illustrating their ability to read Liverpool's passing lanes. Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori remained vertically compact, ensuring Isak had no room to turn or run into channels. This forced Liverpool wide, where Arsenal felt comfortable defending the box.

In possession, Arsenal were direct and purposeful. The winning goal in the 16th minute was a tactical archetype: Rice finding the space to provide the assist for Havertz, who exploited a momentary lapse in Liverpool's central marking. Havertz functioned as a 'false nine' who could drop deep to create a midfield overload or push onto the last man to stretch the defense. By utilising Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis as hardworking wingers who tracked back diligently, Arteta ensured that Liverpool's full-backs, particularly Kerkez, were never allowed to create two-on-one situations. It was a performance of supreme tactical maturity, prioritising the scoreline over aesthetic dominance.

The decisive battle took place in the 'Zone 14' area - the space just outside the penalty box. Liverpool's system is designed to feed Wirtz in this area, but Arteta's decision to use a double pivot of Rice and Guimaraes effectively shuttered this corridor. The statistical evidence is stark: despite 18 shots, Liverpool only managed four efforts on target. This indicates that while Liverpool could reach the final third, they were forced into low-probability shots from distance or headers under extreme pressure.

Arteta won the tactical battle by identifying that Liverpool's greatest weakness under Iraola is their vulnerability to patient, vertical counters. By conceding possession, Arsenal drew Liverpool's mid-block forward, creating the very space Havertz needed for the opening goal. Once ahead, Arsenal's switch to a deeper block dared Liverpool to beat them in the air - a challenge Gabriel and Calafiori met with 17 clearances. Iraola's insistence on crossing (33 total) played directly into Arsenal's hands, representing a failure to adapt to the physical profile of the Gunners' backline.

Iraola recognized the stagnation of his attack relatively early. In the 59th minute, he replaced Nyoni with Dominik Szoboszlai, attempting to add more athleticism and direct running to the midfield. Further changes in the 67th and 81st minutes saw the introduction of Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas, and Lewis Koumas. These substitutions shifted Liverpool toward a more aggressive, almost 4-2-4 shape in the closing stages. While this increased the volume of pressure, it did not improve the quality of chances, as Arsenal's structure remained unyielding.

Arteta's responses were purely reactive and aimed at preservation. The introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly for Guimaraes in the 62nd minute fortified the left side, though the youngster's yellow card in the 72nd minute added tension. Arteta later moved to a five-man defense by bringing on Piero Hincapie for Havertz in the 84th minute, effectively killing the game. The substitution of Mikel Merino for Martin Oedegaard in the 88th minute further reinforced the central block. These tweaks ensured that despite Liverpool's late flurry of corners, David Raya was rarely forced into a difficult save, perfectly executing the game-state management Arteta demanded.

Ultimately, the match was decided by Arsenal's superior defensive floor and Liverpool's lack of a 'Plan B' when central avenues were blocked. Arteta's tactical gamble to cede the ball and rely on structural integrity paid dividends, as Liverpool's 18 shots yielded almost no genuine threat. The 16th-minute goal from Havertz allowed Arsenal to retreat into a shape that Liverpool simply could not dismantle. By forcing the hosts into wide areas and winning the aerial duel in the box, Arsenal's tactical discipline turned Anfield from a cauldron into a stalemate, securing a vital three points.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson 1-yard TD gives Vikings 7-3 lead over Lions
articles.summary: Justin Jefferson has made it to the end zone.
articles.body:
Justin Jefferson has made it to the end zone.

Kyler Murray hit Jefferson for a 1-yard touchdown early in the second quarter, giving the Vikings a 7-3 advantage.

Jefferson was matched up one-on-one on the left side, and was able to tip the fade pass to himself, diving to secure the catch.

It was Jefferson's fourth touchdown of the season and his first reception of the contest.

Murray has now started the game 4-of-9 for 62 yards with a TD.

The Vikings could've scored in the first quarter, but Will Reichard missed a 57-yard field goal wide right.

Additionally, Detroit receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had to be checked in the locker room after going down on what was eventually ruled an incomplete pass in the end zone. But he was back on the sideline and on the field for the next possession.

articles.title: Cowboys Injury Woes Mount As Schoonmaker, Clark Face Sunday Test
articles.summary: Two key starters face uncertainty for Sunday's game against Arizona. Get the latest injury updates and what it means for the Cowboys' run game.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are looking for their first back-to-back wins of the season, but a fresh wave of injuries threatens to derail that momentum just before kickoff. Two key starters are now on the injury report ahead of the Sunday showdown with the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. The situation is fluid, with the team releasing updated practice participation numbers on Friday that leave the coaching staff with tough choices.

Defensive tackle Kenny Clark is the most pressing concern for the front seven. He practiced without issues earlier in the week but was limited on Friday due to a back problem. The defensive line's interior remains uncertain as his status is now listed as questionable. On the other side of the ball, tight end Luke Schoonmaker is expected to miss his third straight game. Thursday and Friday practice sessions were missed due to a groin injury, with reports suggesting he is unlikely to play. This leaves the third-string tight end spot empty just as the team tries to find its offensive identity.

Defensive Health Improves While Offense Struggles

While the loss of Clark and Schoonmaker stings, there is genuine hope on the defensive side of the ball. Three players who have been on injured reserve are finally getting back on the field. Friday's practice saw full participation from Safety P.J. Locke, linebacker Marist Liufau, and defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. They are working through their 21-day practice windows and are listed as questionable for the game. Coach Brian Schottenheimer sees this return as a major turning point for the unit. "The health of this defense is getting us excited. We're getting bodies back, and that's huge for us," Schottenheimer said, according to Yahoo Sports .

These defensive players were needed back after the unit surrendered more than 330 yards in each of the previous two contests. The return of Locke, Liufau, and Bullard adds depth that the team desperately needed. However, the offensive line still faces questions with George Pickens also listed as questionable due to shoulder and hamstring issues. Pickens was limited all week, adding another layer of uncertainty to the receiving corps.

The Cowboys are trying to re-identify who they want to be after a strong 38-21 win over the Eagles. Dak Prescott observed that earlier weeks saw the team lean too heavily on the pass, though the running game offered needed balance. Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 155 yards in that victory. If Schoonmaker cannot play, the team may have to lean even more on the run game and the fullback position. Coach Schottenheimer highlighted fullback Hunter Luepke as a key player to step up if the tight end depth is depleted.

"He's a guy that we talk a lot about that does just everything good," Schottenheimer said regarding Luepke, according to Dallas News . The coach added that Luepke received a game ball for being dominant on special teams against the Eagles last week. This could mean more three-tight-end sets or heavy packages featuring Luepke to compensate for the loss of the tight end depth. Dallas cannot risk another home loss since Arizona has claimed victory in the last four meetings against the Cowboys.

Although Arizona arrives with a 2-5 record, they defeated Dallas 27-17 last season on Monday night. Prescott has not forgotten that loss and emphasized the need to treat the Cardinals with respect. "Understanding what happened last year, it was an ugly, ugly game, ugly on our part," Prescott told DallasCowboys.com this week, according to Yahoo Sports . He described the recent win as a reset and believes the team is ready for the blitz looks Arizona will bring. The game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, and the health of the roster will be the biggest factor in whether Dallas can finally get over the hump.

articles.title: Iraola to tell Alexander Isak to go to ground next time as Liverpool denied 'clear penalty' in Arsenal loss
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola was out-scrapped by his old pal as Mikel Arteta as Liverpool scratched and clawed but couldn't find an equalizer in a tight and tense 1-0 loss...
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola was out-scrapped by his old pal as Mikel Arteta as Liverpool scratched and clawed but couldn't find an equalizer in a tight and tense 1-0 loss to Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday.

But might it have been 1-1 earlier in the game had Alexander Isak dove to the ground after a clear shirt pull slowed his attempted header of a free kick?

Iraola thinks so, and is lamenting his team's failure to turn dominance into goals, including that non-penalty. Iraola said he'll tell Isak to go to the ground next time, calling the fact that Isak not winning a penalty in part because he didn't dive is "a problem for the game."

The loss leaves Liverpool nine points off the top of the table on a day they could've put themselves into the title conversation by moving three back of Man City and Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola reaction from Liverpool's tight clash with Arsenal

Thoughts on the game: "I liked the attitude. Probably our worst part was until we conceded a goal. The reaction to that was very good. We put them under pressure and had some good chances but couldn't find the equalizer."

Why couldn't you finish chances? "You have to give credit to them. The goal comes when we mess up a goal kick and we still had possession to defend it a lot better. We had 7-8 guys but didn't defend it properly. The players then gave everything."

"There were long periods where we pressed really well, really high. When you are losing 1-0 it gives you less merit because they can be on the defensive side. We won a lot of duels against them and I cannot ask more of my players' willingness to go."

"We had big chances. We hit the cross bar. We had real good chances. We should finish better. This is easy to see but the reason was the start of the game that put them in a big advantage,."

Should you have had a penalty? "The Gakpo one was sustained holding but definitely the Alex [Isak] one was a clear one. They hold the tee shirt and he's going to head the ball in but he doesn't go to the ground."

Should he have gone to the ground? "That's the probnlmwe have in the game because he doesn't dive — the fact that you are asking if he should go to the floor. It is what it is. I should tell Alex next time he has to go to the floor."

Will you tell him that? "Yes definitely."

articles.title: When will the Golden State Valkyries parade be? Here's what to know
articles.summary: After Golden State Valkyries achieved an historic win, beating the Atlanta Dream, 68-63, Saturday night at Ballhalla, the team announced details of their cha...
articles.body:
After Golden State Valkyries achieved an historic win, beating the Atlanta Dream, 68-63, Saturday night at Ballhalla, the team announced details of their championship parade!

The Valkyries and the City of San Francisco will host the parade along the city's Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 1.

Fans can begin lining up along the parade route at 9 a.m. on the bay Side of the Embarcadero.

The parade will start at noon and expected to end at 2 p.m.

The parade will start at noon at the Ferry Building, travel along the Embarcadero, and end at King and 2nd streets.

If I can't watch in person, how can I watch?

Viewers can watch coverage on TV on ABC7, or stream on the free ABC7 Bay Area streaming and mobile app starting at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday.

The team, coaches, staff and city leaders will all be there to celebrate the historic win.

According to the Golden State Valkyries, Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, and city officials from across the Bay, are expected to be at the championship parade.

Gabby Williams, who was named WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player, will bang the GSV drum alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie to start the parade, the team said.

Fan opportunities will include a viewing area, presented by OLLY, a championship merchandise truck, and various fan activation zones along the parade route.

Street Closures and Public Transportation

Fans and workers in the area are encouraged to take public transportation such as BART and Muni due to some street closures.

The following streets will be closed from 12:01 a.m. to 4:00 PM on November 4

Eastbound King Street and Northbound Embarcadero between Third Street (at King Street) and Broadway (at Embarcadero)

Market Street between Drumm Street and Steuart Street

Steuart Street between Market Street and southerly terminus

Spear Street between Market Street and southerly terminus

The following streets will be closed from 8:00 a.m. to 4 p.m. on November 4

Southbound Embarcadero and Westbound King between Broadway (at Embarcadero) and Third Street (at King Street)

Washington Street between Drumm Street and the Embarcadero

Mission, Howard, Folsom, Harrison and Bryant streets between Main Street and the Embarcadero

Brannan Street between Second Street and the Embarcadero, with local access maintained to Delancey Street

Townsend Street between Third Street and the Embarcadero

Second Street between Brannan Street and King Street

BART and Muni Metro riders can exit at Embarcadero or Montgomery stations and walk to the parade route. BART will run additional trains and increase staffing and security to accommodate parade-day crowds. For the latest service information and travel updates, visit bart.gov/valkyries .

Muni service on the F and N lines along the Embarcadero will be suspended from approximately 9:30 AM to 3:00 PM.

Alternate service for Muni streetcars along the Embarcadero will be provided by the 15 Bayview Hunters Point Express bus that will be rerouted onto Second Street and pick up at the following locations:

Northbound Fourth Street and Townsend Street

Third Street between Townsend Street and Brannan Street

Second Street between Brannan Street and Bryant Street

Southbound Second Street between Market Street and Mission Street

Muni ambassadors will be on site at affected stops to direct passengers to alternative locations. For all transit and traffic updates, please visit

City partners have worked in close coordination withautonomous vehicleoperatorsto reduce congestion in dense, high-foot traffic zones around the parade route. Autonomous vehicle operations will be restricted in the following areas from 12:01 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. on November 4:

On the Embarcadero, south of Battery Street

In the Financial District, streets south of Washington Street and east of Battery Street

In the South of Market, streets east of First Street

Bryant Street between Second Street and the Embarcadero

Brannan Street between Third Street and the Embarcadero

King Street between Fifth Street and the Embarcadero

Berry Street between Fifth Street and Third Street

Second Street between Bryant Street and King Street

Third Street between Brannan Street and Mission Creek Channel

Fourth Street between Townsend Street and Mission Creek Channel

Autonomous vehicle riders will see available pickup and drop-off locations in their respective phone apps. Pick-up and drop-off will be restricted on the following streets:

Battery Street between the Embarcadero and Market Street

First Street between Market Street and Harrison Street

Third Street between Folsom Street and Brannan Street

Fourth Street between Harrison Street and Townsend Street
